subject.title: fix(ci): sweep PRs with unknown mergeability in pr-ci-sweeper

question: Should the existing destructive CI-recovery automation be allowed to close/reopen PRs while GitHub reports mergeability as unknown, relying on the existing per-PR budget and post-reopen conflict recomputation?
rationale: The code change is narrow, but it deliberately changes the safety threshold for a workflow that mutates other contributors’ PR lifecycle state; protected `maintainer` handling and rollout ownership require an explicit human choice.

options.title: Land with monitored rollout
options.body: Merge the bounded guard change and have the feature owner monitor an immediate live dispatch for the named dropped-CI population, retaining redacted output that CI attaches to their current heads.

options.title: Keep the pending guard
options.body: Retain the current conservative skip until maintainers have a safer way to distinguish a permanently stuck merge-ref computation from a transient unknown conflict.

options.title: Add a narrower diagnostic gate
options.body: Revise the sweeper to require an additional observable stuck-state signal before re-firing unknown mergeability, then rerun focused tests and review the new failure mode.

recommendation.title: Land with monitored rollout
recommendation.body: Merge the bounded guard change and have the feature owner monitor an immediate live dispatch for the named dropped-CI population, retaining redacted output that CI attaches to their current heads.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the merged sweeper and documented the production probes that motivate this follow-up.
